title: Metrics label normalization, compact event compressor, and lightweight log path
creator: Daniel Carter
description: Address long-running metrics and logging inefficiencies by: 1) normalizing metric label schemas across services to reduce cardinality and costly aggregation paths; 2) introducing a compact event compressor for high-frequency telemetry events (prefix dedupe + delta-encoding) to cut network and storage overhead; 3) replacing a heavy, sync logging dependency in the runtime hot-path with a lightweight, async log forwarder. Goal is measurable p95 latency and CPU reductions under typical inference workloads.
background: Over the last 12 months we've observed sustained increases in Prometheus scrape times and downstream storage costs driven by label explosion and repeated high-cardinality event payloads. Concurrently, a synchronous logging library used in the runtime contributes to CPU stalls during burst traffic. Prior tickets (ENG-703211, ENG-406789) focused on tracing batchers and exporter convergence but did not address label schema drift nor event payload size. This ticket consolidates schema and runtime logging changes to reduce resource usage while keeping observability fidelity.
proposal: 1) Define a canonical metrics label schema (service, route, model_id, shard=null when absent) and a migration guide for instrumented services. 2) Implement a compact event compressor as a middleware in the telemetry gateway: it will do prefix de-duplication, integer delta-encoding for timestamps and token counts, and optional gzip fallback for large events. 3) Swap the synchronous logger in the runtime hot path for 'mini-forwarder' (small in-process async buffer + background flush to telemetry gateway) with backpressure and bounded memory. 4) Expose a rollout flag and telemetry to validate fidelity against raw streams for 2 weeks before full cutover.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical label schema published and accepted by platform & two major services
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating <10% deviation in key observability alerts when compressor is enabled
Telemetry gateway CPU or egress reduced by >=30% on a representative workload with compressor enabled
Runtime p95 latency improved by >=8% under synthetic burst traffic after replacing logger
Graceful fallback path: if compressor fails, telemetry is still forwarded uncompressed for a short window
Migration runbook included and stakeholders trained (platform, infra, client SDK owners)
rollout_plan: 1) Week 0: Publish schema doc and linting rules. 2) Week 1: Instrumentation changes in 2 canary services with feature flag. 3) Week 2: Deploy event compressor at telemetry gateway with feature flag; monitor cardinality and storage. 4) Week 3: Replace runtime logger in a small quota pool; observe p95. 5) Week 4: Gradual ramp to 50% traffic with automated rollback if error rate or metric divergence exceeds threshold. 6) Week 5: Full cutover and deprecate old logging path.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Compressor changes could distort metric semantics -> Mitigation: Maintain raw capture for 48h in parallel and run fidelity checks
Risk: Label normalization breaks dashboards/alerts -> Mitigation: Provide compatibility transforms in query layer for 2 months
Risk: Memory amplification in async forwarder -> Mitigation: Bounded ring buffer + circuit-breaker + OOM monitoring
Risk: Increased CPU at telemetry gateway during compression -> Mitigation: Use adaptive sampling; benchmarking before rollout
testing_plan: Unit tests for compressor algorithms, integration tests with telemetry gateway, regression tests comparing alerting signal before/after for key dashboards, load tests simulating 10k rps with realistic label distributions, and canary on 'internal-dev' environment for 72h. Add a synthetic job that asserts cardinality and event-size percentiles every 5m.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with platform and two service owners (search-service, routing). Action: agree on initial label set and sticky fallback tag.
2026-03-05: Drafted canonical label JSON schema in Confluence and added prometheus-lint rule prototype. Assigned SDK owners to adopt in their next minor release.

2026-03-07: Implemented compressor prototype (delta + prefix dedupe). Benchmarks on dev: 45% median event size reduction, 28% CPU increase on single-threaded compressor process. Decided to move compressor to multi-threaded worker pool.
2026-03-11: Runtime logger replacement branch opened (PR 4021). Early microbench: allocated goroutines reduced during hot-path by 60% and p95 CPU lowered by ~10% in microbench harness.
2026-03-13: Integration smoke tests passed in staging. Noted small divergence (4%) in a top-level alert; added compensating mapping rule in query layer. Planning canary for 2026-03-16.
notes: Keep telemetry fidelity checks public and automated. Coordinate with billing team to measure downstream storage delta. Communicate changes on #observability slack channel and schedule a 30m demo after canary. Consider adding a deprecation timeline for old high-cardinality labels to encourage owners to migrate.
